title: AAC vs MP3: Which Audio Format Should You Choose?
description: Choose AAC for efficient encoding or MP3 for broad compatibility. Compare quality, file size and re-encoding, then make a sharing copy on iPhone.
direct: Use AAC if the recipient supports it. Choose MP3 if the upload form or player asks for it. Keep your best original for future conversions.

cards.aac.heading: AAC: efficient encoding
cards.aac.body: AAC can preserve slightly more quality than MP3 at a similar file size, depending on the encoder and material. It is a useful listening-copy choice for compatible devices.
cards.mp3.heading: MP3: broad compatibility
cards.mp3.body: Use MP3 when the destination requests .mp3 or you need a copy for a player that does not accept AAC. Check the actual receiving requirements first.
sections.size.heading: Will AAC always make a smaller file?
sections.size.body: No. Duration and total bitrate determine most of the encoded size. Ten minutes at a constant 128 kbps is about 9.6 MB before headers and metadata, whichever codec you choose. AAC efficiency is a quality tradeoff, not an automatic size reduction. For the calculation, see our audio bitrate guide below.
sections.original.heading: Keep the original before converting
sections.original.body: Converting AAC to MP3, or MP3 to AAC, cannot recover discarded detail. Another lossy encode can reduce quality. Export from the best available original and listen to speech, music and quiet passages in the copy before sharing.
sections.mac.heading: A desktop option
sections.mac.body: On Mac, Apple Music can convert eligible local files with its AAC or MP3 encoder. That is an alternative if the files are already on your computer. Apple limits conversion of iTunes Store purchases to iTunes Plus songs.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: What should I check when comparing two speech exports?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Listen for fuzzy consonants, metallic sounds around breaths and changes in quiet pauses. Compare the same passage at a similar listening volume.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: An older player lists MP3. Should I send AAC anyway?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Send a real MP3 copy and test it on that player. Keep the AAC source so that a compatibility copy does not become your only archive.
